# Work Loop v2 Codex usage optimization report

**Date:** 2026-08-13  
**Decision mode:** Deterministic changes only; no trials or A/B testing  
**Scope:** Codex usage generated by Work Loop v2, especially with GPT-5.6 Sol at high reasoning

## Executive conclusion

Work Loop v2 is consuming usage quickly because several multipliers are stacking:

1. The dispatcher inherits the global `gpt-5.6-sol` + `high` configuration for every Codex hop.
2. Every fresh Codex process loads a large fixed instruction package before reading the task itself.
3. The dispatcher can automatically repeat a failed Codex hop even when the first model request actually ran.
4. The unattended loop permits four hops although the normal prepared-brief path should close in three.
5. Long interactive sessions repeatedly send an expanding conversation and tool history.

The most important finding is that **input context, not visible answer length or reasoning output, is the dominant usage driver**. A representative fresh dispatcher session recorded 137,787 input tokens, of which 119,808 were cached, versus 1,800 output tokens and 652 reasoning-output tokens. An independent longer Work Loop session accumulated 3.9 million input tokens, and another accumulated 17.3 million. Cached input is cheaper, but it is not free.

I recommend a fixed operating policy:

> Run routine Work Loop Codex hops on **GPT-5.6 Terra with medium reasoning**. Permit **Sol/high only through an explicit exception flag** for predefined high-consequence or unusually ambiguous assessments.

Then remove accidental extra hops and compress the always-loaded Work Loop context. This is a higher-return sequence than tuning answer verbosity, changing timeouts, or relying on prompt caching.

## What the evidence says

### 1. Work Loop silently inherits the most expensive routine configuration

The user-level Codex configuration selects `gpt-5.6-sol` with `model_reasoning_effort = "high"`. The Work Loop dispatcher invokes `codex exec` without a model or reasoning override, so each Codex assessment inherits those settings.

Codex supports both controls at invocation time:

```text
codex exec --model gpt-5.6-terra \
  --config 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' ...
```

This makes the correction local to Work Loop. It does not change how Codex behaves in unrelated tasks and follows this repository's policy of per-command model tiering rather than global defaults.

OpenAI positions Sol as the flagship model and Terra as the intelligence/cost-balanced model. Its current Codex credit table charges Terra at 40% of Sol's rate for input, cached input, and output tokens. Therefore, **Terra is 60% cheaper per token at equal token volume**. That is an exact rate comparison, not a promise of a 60% end-to-end reduction because models can generate different token volumes. See [Codex pricing and usage](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing) and [GPT-5.6 model guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model).

OpenAI describes medium reasoning as the balanced starting point and recommends high or xhigh only when the additional reasoning produces a measured quality gain. Since this plan deliberately excludes trials, Work Loop should use a predefined task-class rule instead of dynamic experimentation.

### 2. The fixed instruction payload is much larger than the task prompt suggests

The two mandatory Work Loop runtime documents currently total approximately:

| Runtime input | Lines | Words | Bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `.agents/skills/work-loop-v2/SKILL.md` | 608 | 10,695 | 66,636 |
| `plans/work-loop-v2-mvp/work-loop-v2-executable-core-v0.1.md` | 475 | 4,183 | 24,476 |
| **Combined** | **1,083** | **14,878** | **91,112** |

The selected skill must be read in full. When Work Loop owns the request, the skill also directs Codex to resolve and read the executable core. A short courier prompt therefore starts a much larger model session than its visible text implies.

OpenAI's current guidance says to state each instruction once, expose only relevant tools, and keep tool descriptions concise. In its internal coding-agent sample, leaner system prompts used 41–66% fewer total tokens and 33–67% less cost while improving scores by roughly 10–15%. OpenAI labels those ranges directional rather than guaranteed. See [GPT-5.6 prompting guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model#prompting-best-practices).

### 3. Repeated input dominates reasoning output

Local Codex session traces show the shape of the problem:

| Session shape | Input tokens | Cached input | Output | Reasoning output | Observation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Fresh noninteractive Work Loop hop | 137,787 | 119,808 | 1,800 | 652 | About 87% of input was cached, but all repeated context still counted |
| Independent Work Loop session | 3,903,157 | 3,608,320 | 17,892 | 7,773 | Final individual call had about 112k input |
| Long interactive Work Loop session | 17,302,287 | 16,214,784 | 104,530 | 45,476 | Final individual call had about 121k input |

The totals are cumulative request usage recorded in the session JSONL. They should not be translated directly into a precise ChatGPT plan percentage because subscription metering, caching, and concurrent sessions complicate that conversion. They do establish the mechanism: every new model/tool turn reprocesses a large context, so long sessions compound usage quickly.

Three older dispatcher output samples show the same pattern, averaging roughly 218k input tokens versus 4.2k output tokens, with a 77% cached-input share. The Work Loop skill was materially shorter at that time, so those samples do not establish a safe ceiling for the current runtime.

### 4. Automatic retry can pay twice for one assessment

The dispatcher retries a failed actor hop once when the repository is unchanged. A nonzero exit does not prove that the model request never started. The first process may already have consumed its input and reasoning budget before a transport, parsing, or finalization failure.

This also conflicts with the Work Loop contract's stricter rule: rerun the same hop only when the dispatcher log proves the first launch never started. The correct operational distinction is not “did the repo change?” but “did a model request begin and consume usage?”

### 5. The normal path does not need four hops

From a prepared brief, the normal unattended sequence is:

1. Claude implements.
2. Codex assesses.
3. Claude closes or repairs and closes.

The dispatcher's default maximum of four hops allows one more actor launch than this standard path requires. A larger ceiling is useful for explicit recovery, but it should not be the routine default.

## Recommended fix package

The percentages below must not be added together. Each fix affects a partly overlapping portion of usage.

### P0 — Apply immediately

#### Fix 1: Pin routine Work Loop Codex hops to Terra/medium

**Change**

- Add dispatcher options such as `--codex-model` and `--codex-effort`.
- Set Work Loop's internal defaults to `gpt-5.6-terra` and `medium`.
- Pass both explicitly to `codex exec`.
- Leave the user's global Codex configuration unchanged.
- Record the selected model and effort in the dispatcher log before launch.

**Sol/high exception rule**

Sol/high is permitted only when the task state explicitly marks one of these categories:

- first-time architecture with several consequential, unresolved tradeoffs;
- security, confidentiality, permissions, or destructive-action assessment;
- high-consequence acceptance where a false pass would be expensive;
- an assessment whose evidence is materially contradictory or incomplete and requires inference rather than verification.

Routine spec compliance, evidence checking, bounded code review, repair assessment, routing, and closure remain Terra/medium. The operator can force Sol/high with an explicit dispatcher flag; there is no automatic promotion and no trial phase.

**Expected return**

- 60% lower Codex credit rate per token for the affected hops at current published rates.
- Additional savings from medium versus high reasoning, although the exact reduction is task-dependent.

**Risk control**

- The exception rule preserves Sol/high for work where extra depth is inherently justified.
- The assessment contract and evidence requirements do not change.

#### Fix 2: Remove automatic retry after any live model request

**Change**

- Delete the “repo unchanged, retry once” rule for actor failures.
- Retry automatically only when logs prove the process failed before a Codex request began—for example, binary-not-found, invalid preflight configuration, or another zero-token launch failure.
- If a model request began, stop the run and report the failure. Resumption must create a new, explicit hop.
- Persist the Codex session/run identifier and final usage event so the dispatcher can make this determination mechanically.

**Expected return**

- Prevents a failed Codex hop from silently doubling its model usage.
- Restores alignment with the Work Loop's existing no-duplicate-hop contract.

#### Fix 3: Change the unattended default from four hops to three

**Change**

- Set `max_hops=3` for a run that starts from a prepared brief.
- Require an explicit override for recovery or a task state that already proves another hop is necessary.
- Stop rather than improvise when the cap is reached.

**Expected return**

- Removes 25% of the routine maximum launch allowance.
- Prevents unclear state from turning into another expensive actor call.

### P1 — Structural high-return work

#### Fix 4: Compress the always-loaded Work Loop runtime

**Change**

Refactor the current 91KB skill-plus-core hot path into:

1. a short router that determines whether Work Loop owns the request;
2. a compact executable contract containing only invariants, state transitions, evidence rules, and output schema;
3. conditional references for rationale, examples, history, rare recovery procedures, courier variants, and the full routing catalog.

The hot path should state each rule once. A summary placed above the existing long files is insufficient because Codex must still read a selected `SKILL.md` completely.

Set a mechanical size budget for the always-loaded pair. I would use **24KB combined as the initial hard ceiling**: large enough to retain the executable contract, but roughly one quarter of today's payload. This number is a design constraint, not a claim that 24KB is mathematically optimal.

**Expected return**

- Attacks the fixed input charged on every fresh Codex hop.
- Makes prompt-cache misses less costly.
- Aligns with OpenAI's strongest documented token-efficiency lever for coding agents.

#### Fix 5: Add a dedicated dispatcher-hop execution path

**Change**

When Codex is launched by the dispatcher, the skill should enter an explicit noninteractive path:

- read the compact Work Loop contract once;
- read the exact task-state file named in the courier prompt;
- read only the evidence paths named by that state;
- do not scan sibling state files;
- do not perform generic reorientation;
- do not reread the governing plan or current-state documents unless the task state marks a material context change;
- do not rerun Claude's verification unless one of the Work Loop's existing four evidence exceptions applies;
- return one structured verdict and one state update.

Deterministic routing, file discovery, repository-change checks, and bookkeeping belong in the shell dispatcher, not in additional model turns.

**Expected return**

- Reduces both input tokens and model/tool round trips.
- Prevents routine courier hops from paying for interactive recovery behavior.

#### Fix 6: Put a size budget on the active task-state file

**Change**

- Warn when the state file exceeds 12KB.
- Refuse the next unattended hop when it exceeds 16KB until it is compacted.
- Keep only current objective, acceptance criteria, decision state, evidence pointers, blockers, and next action.
- Link to existing evidence artifacts rather than pasting test logs, diffs, or resolved discussion into the state file.
- Preserve decisions and negative constraints; remove superseded narration.

The thresholds are proposed guardrails, not experimentally derived constants. Their purpose is to stop unbounded growth while leaving enough room for a complete bounded-unit record.

**Expected return**

- Caps the variable context repeated on every subsequent hop.
- Improves reliability by making the state file a decision record rather than a transcript.

### P2 — Enforcement and visibility

#### Fix 7: Turn usage telemetry into a circuit breaker

**Change**

- Parse the `turn.completed.usage` event already emitted by `codex exec --json`.
- Record input, cached input, output, and reasoning-output tokens for each Codex hop.
- Show per-hop and cumulative-run usage in the dispatcher summary.
- Stop before another actor launch when the configured Codex run budget has been exhausted.
- Require an explicit operator override to continue.

The budget should initially be expressed as **one routine Codex assessment hop per bounded unit**, not as a guessed subscription percentage. Raw token counts do not map cleanly to the app's rolling allowance, but the dispatcher can reliably prevent duplicate or additional hops.

**Expected return**

- Does not itself reduce tokens, but makes the P0 controls enforceable.
- Prevents silent continuation after an unexpectedly large assessment.

#### Fix 8: Preserve cache-friendly ordering after compression

**Change**

- Put the stable, compact instruction prefix first.
- Append task-specific state, paths, timestamps, and evidence afterward.
- Keep the tool/schema declaration stable between equivalent dispatcher hops.
- Monitor cached-input tokens, but treat caching as a secondary optimization.

OpenAI documents that prompt-cache hits require exact prefix matches. See [Prompt caching](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching).

**Expected return**

- Lowers the price of the remaining repeated input.
- Does not replace context removal because cached input still consumes credits.

## Implementation order

This should be executed as one deterministic correction program, not as a sequence of trials.

### Change set A — Immediate containment

1. Add explicit Terra/medium dispatcher arguments and the Sol/high override.
2. Replace live-request retry with zero-token preflight retry only.
3. Set the prepared-brief default to three hops.
4. Parse and print Codex usage after every hop.

### Change set B — Remove structural waste

1. Extract conditional reference material from the Work Loop skill and core.
2. Enforce the 24KB combined hot-path ceiling.
3. Add the dispatcher-specific noninteractive path.
4. Add task-state warning and stop thresholds.
5. Stabilize the prompt prefix.

### Change set C — Verification without trials

No live comparative workloads are required. Verify implementation with deterministic checks:

- inspect the constructed command and assert that routine runs contain Terra/medium;
- assert that the explicit exception produces Sol/high;
- use a fake Codex executable to prove that preflight failure may retry but a started request may not;
- assert that prepared-brief runs stop at three hops;
- fixture-test JSONL usage parsing and budget stops;
- fail a static size check if the hot-path documents exceed 24KB combined;
- fail a state-file check at the 16KB unattended ceiling;
- confirm that the assessment schema and Work Loop state transitions are unchanged.

These are implementation tests, not usage trials: they prove the controls behave as specified without spending model allowance comparing configurations.

## What not to do

- **Do not change the global Codex model setting.** Work Loop should own its own tiering, and unrelated work may still justify Sol/high.
- **Do not make Luna the general assessor.** It is attractive for high-volume, known-shape tasks, but Terra/medium is the safer fixed default for judgment-heavy review.
- **Do not increase timeouts.** A longer timeout does not reduce input and can allow an expensive stuck path to continue.
- **Do not rely on caching alone.** Representative Work Loop sessions were already heavily cached and still consumed usage quickly.
- **Do not add telemetry without stop rules.** Reporting usage after an overrun is weaker than preventing the next launch.
- **Do not shorten visible answers as the main fix.** Output is a small share of the measured Work Loop token volume.
- **Do not add another summary document while retaining the full mandatory runtime.** The selected skill would still load both.
- **Do not introduce an A/B test, pilot, or trial phase.** The chosen defaults are based on current official model positioning, rate differences, observed local usage shape, and reversible per-command configuration.

## Expected outcome

The immediate package should materially slow allowance consumption even before the structural rewrite:

- routine token-unit cost falls by 60% at current rates when moving from Sol to Terra;
- high reasoning is removed from routine assessments;
- duplicate live-model retry is eliminated;
- the maximum normal path is reduced from four launches to three.

The structural package then reduces the number of tokens to which those rates apply. The largest uncertainty is the exact end-to-end percentage because ChatGPT plan metering is not a simple API bill and token volume can change by task. That uncertainty does not weaken the decision: every recommended change removes a known multiplier while retaining a clear Sol/high escape hatch.

## Decision requested

Approve the package as the Work Loop v2 operating policy:

1. **Terra/medium by default; Sol/high only by explicit exception.**
2. **No automatic retry after a model request starts.**
3. **Three-hop default from a prepared brief.**
4. **24KB maximum always-loaded Work Loop runtime.**
5. **12KB state warning and 16KB unattended stop.**
6. **One routine Codex assessment per bounded unit, enforced through JSONL usage accounting.**

This package does not require the operator to conduct trials. It is reversible through explicit flags, but the defaults are decisive.
